item.research_question: How can short-range order (SRO) be detected in medium/high-entropy alloys (MEAs/HEAs) using non-imaging and imaging techniques, and what is the impact of SRO on their physical and mechanical properties?
item.material_system: NiCoCr medium-entropy alloy (MEA), CrMnFeCoNi and CrFeCoNiPd high-entropy alloys (HEAs), VNiCo MEA, Ru-based HEA nanoparticles (NPs), and a 15-element HEA (15-HEA)
item.processing_route: Synthesis of NiCoCr samples followed by two heat treatments: water-quenching after homogenization at 1,200°C, and aging at 1,000°C for 120 h followed by slow furnace cooling; synthesis of VNiCo MEA; synthesis of Ru-based HEA NPs via carbothermal shock; irradiation of NiCoCr with Ni ions at doses up to 0.3 displacements per atoms (dpa)
item.test_conditions: X-ray diffraction (XRD), neutron diffraction, X-ray absorption spectroscopy (XAS/EXAFS), transmission electron microscopy (TEM), high-angle annular dark-field scanning TEM (HAADF-STEM), energy-dispersive spectroscopy (EDS), geometric phase analysis (GPA), nano-indentation, bulk tensile tests, and irradiation tests
key_findings: In NiCoCr MEA, EXAFS fitting revealed that Cr atoms favored bonding with Ni and Co atoms, while Cr-Cr bonds were disfavored, indicated by a larger Debye-Waller (DW) factor for Cr-Cr bonds compared to Cr-Ni and Cr-Co bonds.

Aging NiCoCr MEA at 1,000°C for 120 h followed by slow cooling resulted in superlattice streaking in diffraction patterns and contrast in dark-field images, indicating increased SRO compared to water-quenched samples.
In VNiCo MEA, EDS mapping showed an alternating pattern of V-enriched regions sandwiching Co- or Ni-enriched regions, with a spacing of less than 1 nm, confirming SRO.
Irradiation of NiCoCr MEA to 0.3 dpa decreased Ni-Cr bond distances from 2.51 Å to 2.49 Å and reduced DW factors from 0.002 Å² to 0.001 Å², suggesting radiation increases the amount of SRO.
The aged NiCoCr MEA showed a 25% increase in yield point compared to the water-quenched sample, confirming the strengthening effect of SRO.
The stacking fault energy (SFE) for the aged NiCoCr sample was double that of the water-quenched sample, indicating a positive correlation between SRO degree and SFE.
In VNiCo MEA, SRO-dislocation coupling was observed, where dislocations were sluggish through SRO domains, leading to increased strain hardening during tensile deformation.
APT analysis of annealed NiCoCr MEA showed peak intensity variations spanning approximately 2 nm, classified as local chemical ordering (LCO) rather than typical SRO.
item.mechanism: SRO arises from preferential bonding between specific elements (e.g., Cr-Ni/Co in NiCoCr, V-Co/Ni in VNiCo), leading to local lattice distortions and alternating chemical planes. These distortions create energetically favorable domains that impede dislocation motion (SRO-dislocation coupling), increasing yield strength and strain hardening. Radiation exposure can enhance SRO by altering bond distances and reducing lattice disorder.
item.limitations: XRD and neutron diffraction total scattering measurements were not able to identify evidence of ordering in NiCoCr MEA because PDF analysis could not distinguish bond lengths and vibrations of pairs of atoms with comparable atomic sizes. TEM imaging alone could not determine the exact bonding preferences causing alternating contrast; element-specific methods were required. Most studies focused on MEAs with 3d transition metals, limiting understanding of more complex HEAs with 4d or 5d metals.
item.future_work: Conduct studies on HEA samples containing higher numbers of elements and combinations of 3d, 4d, and 5d transition metals to uncover how SRO arises in a wider compositional space. Prepare samples with varying degrees of SRO through controlled heat treatments to accurately assess the impact of SRO on mechanical properties. Investigate the impact of SRO on the catalytic properties of HEA nanoparticles. Develop new non-imaging and imaging techniques, such as 4D-STEM and atom probe tomography (APT), to better characterize SRO.
quotes: Cr atoms favored bonding with Ni and Co atoms, and disfavored forming bonds with other Cr atoms.
The DW factor for Cr-Cr bonds was found to be larger than for Cr-Ni and Cr-Co bonds.
Aging MEA samples at high temperatures followed by slow cooling allow atoms to have higher mobility, resulting in the evolution of the structure toward a lower free-energy state with more SRO.
